item.title: Presley Gerber, son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, dead at 27
item.description: Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber's son Presley Gerber, who signed with IMG Models and walked for Moschino and Calvin Klein, has died at age 27.
item.content:encoded:
Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, has died. He was 27.

Presley's death was confirmed by Cindy’s representative to Fox News Digital, sharing a statement from the family: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."

According to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner, Gerber died Sunday at a rehabilitation facility.

TMZ noted that an autopsy has yet to be completed.

KAIA GERBER OWNS 'NEPO BABY' STATUS WHILE QUESTIONING OTHER CELEBRITY KIDS: 'SHOW ME WHY YOU DESERVE THIS JOB'

Presley was the only son of Cindy and Rande Gerber and the older brother of model and actress Kaia Gerber.

Presley had been open about his mental health struggles, speaking publicly about them on social media and in interviews.

Kaia spoke about her brother's mental health and drug use to Vogue in a cover story published in August 2026.

Vogue described Presley’s journey as a "decade-long struggle with drug addiction."

KELLY OSBOURNE DRAWS A LINE WITH ESTRANGED SISTER AIMEE: 'I DON'T WANT YOU IN MY LIFE'

Kaia, 24, told the outlet: "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone."

"I think that’s also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help. Because it felt like too much to have two children who were needing," she added.

"My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything—and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone.’ There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them," Kaia told Vogue, referring to Presley's openness on social media about his mental health and drug use struggles.

CARA DELEVINGNE ADMITS SHE USED PARTY DRUG GHB DAILY BEFORE TERRIFYING SEIZURES FORCED HER SOBER

In December 2025, Presley shared an Instagram video — which he later deleted — speaking out about taking medications including Xanax, Valium and buprenorphine while discussing his panic attacks and recovery, according to People magazine.

"Unfortunately, I’ve had a lot of loss in many different forms recently, so that is not an excuse, but it’s the reason why I am where I’m at now," the outlet reported, noting that he said he wanted to reach "people in many ways."

"A. So you feel like you’re not alone, because that is how I feel most of the time and I have a feeling that if I saw all of this, a lot of people will at least know that there’s someone else going through it. And the second thing is, hopefully I find some people out here and are willing to help or know someone that could help," he said, via People.

He also appeared on a Studio 22 podcast in February 2023.

'BAYWATCH: HAWAII' STAR BRANDY LEDFORD SAYS SHE 'WANTED TO TRULY CHECK OUT' BEFORE REHAB SAVED HER LIFE

"Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that’s alI I need to do."

In 2019, Presley was charged with a DUI.

HILARY DUFF, NIKKI GLASER LEAD DARING FASHION ON THE AMERICAN MUSIC AWARDS RED CARPET

HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOS

He signed with IMG Models at age 15 and later walked the runway for several designer houses.

Presley made his runway debut at Moschino's show in Los Angeles in 2016.

He also starred in a campaign for Calvin Klein and a fragrance ad for Celine, as well as appearing in Dolce & Gabbana and Tommy Hilfiger shows.

item.title: Harrison Butker drills game-winner as Chiefs survive overtime thriller against Colts
item.description: Patrick Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns as the Kansas City Chiefs outlasted the Indianapolis Colts in a wild overtime thriller.
item.content:encoded:
The Kansas City Chiefs survived a grueling 33-30 brawl against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night, grinding out a victory that went straight down to the final second of overtime.

Harrison Butker predictably split the uprights to give KC a 30-27 lead in extra time, but Indy stubbornly refused to throw in the towel.

For a tame four quarters, action rocketed in overtime, notably when Colts QB Daniel Jones connected with Laquon Treadwell on a 48-yard bomb deep into Chiefs territory, setting up a game-tying field goal by Spencer Shrader to make it 30-30.

Yes, Laquon Treadwell, of all people — the former Vikings first-rounder out of Ole Miss who never lived up to his draft slot.

Butker ended the chaos on the following drive, drilling a 40-yard game-winner as time expired in extra time.

Following the loss, Daniel Jones fell to an abysmal 1-16 in career primetime starts, and he hasn't tasted a night-game victory since 2022 when he played for New York.

Kansas City couldn't put away the Colts with ease, but they found a way. While Indianapolis searches for answers in 2026, Kansas City is proving the dynasty magic remains very much intact.

Patrick Mahomes carved up Indy, completing 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. Hand-wringing over his mobility headlined the opener against Denver, but Mahomes proved he can dismantle a secondary strictly from the pocket.

"We didn't do exactly what we wanted to do," Mahomes said postgame, while lauding his team's resilience.

COLTS FACE QUARTERBACK UNCERTAINTY AS DANIEL JONES RECOVERS FROM ACHILLES INJURY

Across the sideline, Jones posted an efficient line in defeat for Indy, finishing 22-of-31 for 210 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

Targeting Travis Kelce early and often paid dividends, as the veteran tight end poured in nine catches for 101 yards and a touchdown for KC. Kenneth Walker III chewed up turf on the ground, rushing 24 times for 117 yards.

Naturally, Taylor Swift was in the suite alongside her mother, Andrea, and set the internet on fire by flashing her ring after Kelce scored Kansas City's first touchdown.

Jonathan Taylor was an absolute workhorse for Indianapolis, proving impervious to Steve Spagnuolo’s defense while racking up 132 total yards (92 rushing on 24 carries, four catches for 40 yards) and two touchdowns.

On the injury front, Colts wideout Alec Pierce was forced to leave the game with a heel issue, though initial X-rays came back negative, with further evaluation scheduled for Monday.

Despite falling short, the Colts continue to show a pulse under head coach Shane Steichen, even as general manager Chris Ballard sits on an increasingly scorching hot seat at 0-2.

item.title: Manhunt underway in California after armed suspect allegedly points gun at people, shoots at officers
item.description: California deputies urge local residents to lock their doors amid a manhunt for a suspect wanted for several felonies, including pointing a firearm at people.
item.content:encoded:
Deputies in California are searching for a man believed to be armed and dangerous after allegedly murdering a woman and shooting at others, according to authorities.

Derek Spencer, 44, is wanted for several felonies, including pointing a firearm at people in Placer County on Sunday, according to the Placer County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said Spencer was initially wanted after allegedly pointing a firearm at people earlier Sunday.

During the search for Spencer earlier on Sunday, deputies found him in the Iowa Hill area. Spencer rammed a patrol vehicle before fleeing the area, triggering the manhunt.

DRAMATIC VIDEO SHOWS SWAT VEHICLE RAMMING TRACTOR DURING TENSE OREGON STANDOFF

Spencer also fired shots at law enforcement officers and helicopters assisting law enforcement. No law enforcement officers were injured during the search for Spencer.

Everyone in the Iowa Hill area is urged to lock their doors and remain inside.

In an update on Sunday night, the sheriff's office said the search remained ongoing, noting the search is very challenging due to the area being very large, with dense forest and steep, rugged terrain.

SUSPECT IN DEATHS OF 5 FOUND DEAD AFTER COPS UNCOVER GRIM SCENE AT RURAL PROPERTY OUTSIDE PORTLAND

But during the search, deputies located a murder victim they believe was killed by Spencer.

"As tactical teams worked to clear a home where Spencer had been earlier in the search, they located an adult female who had been shot and killed inside the home. At this point in the investigation, it’s believed Spencer murdered the woman before fleeing into the surrounding forest," deputies said.

The sheriff's office is being assisted by multiple other law enforcement agencies.

"Teams will continue searching throughout the night and will not slow down as we work to locate this armed and very dangerous individual," the sheriff's office said.

The sheriff's office described Spencer as a bald man with a goatee.

item.title: Missing Carnival Panorama passenger jumped overboard off Mexico's coast
item.description: A male passenger jumped overboard from the Carnival Panorama as it sailed from Puerto Vallarta back to Long Beach, triggering a major search.
item.content:encoded:
A passenger traveling on a Carnival Panorama cruise jumped overboard as the ship was wrapping up the last full day of a week-long sailing.

The cruise departed Long Beach, California, on September 13 and was headed back there from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, when a male passenger jumped overboard, according to the cruise line.

"Carnival Cruise Line confirmed Saturday that a male guest aboard Carnival Panorama jumped overboard while the ship was sailing from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico to Long Beach, California," a Carnival Cruise Line spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN

"When notified of a missing guest, the ship's team initiated search and investigation procedures, including reviewing CCTV footage and notifying both the U.S. and Mexico Coast Guards," the statement continued.

The spokesperson said the company is providing support to the family who was traveling with the guest.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with them and their loved ones," the statement reads.

CARNIVAL CRUISE PASSENGER, 67, FOUND DEAD WHILE SNORKELING OFF THE COAST OF AUSTRALIA DURING EXCURSION

According to a Reddit user who said they were aboard the sailing, announcements regarding a missing guest were heard at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Carnival Panorama had departed from its last port of call on the sail, Puerto Vallarta, at 8 p.m. on Thursday.

The call for the missing guest was repeated several times over the next several hours. At about 3 p.m., the ship reportedly turned around.

Another announcement was made at about 3:30 p.m. that there would be a shipwide search, and all guests were told to return to their staterooms. Security visited each of the staterooms to scan guests' ship identification cards, which is a standard procedure in the event of a search.

An hour later, another announcement suggested the search was continuing, and guests were instructed to remain in their staterooms.

At around 5 p.m., the captain and cruise director said the guest had been confirmed overboard after a review of onboard cameras, adding that local authorities would continue the search and rescue operation and guests were no longer required to stay in their staterooms.

The family and traveling companions of the missing guest were notified of his disappearance and were offered support from the care team.

Shortly after 7 p.m., guests were told that the ship was expected to reach Long Beach at 9 a.m.

Fox News' Jessica Mekles contributed to this report.

item.title: Patrick Clancy in his own words: Top takeaways from grieving father's first interview
item.description: Patrick Clancy told "60 Minutes" that baby Callan died in his arms after four agonizing days and recalled apologizing to his son in their final moments.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Clancy begged for just one of his children to survive, held baby Callan as he died in his arms and revealed why he forgave Lindsay after she killed their three children.

Speaking with correspondent Ross Douthat on CBS News' "60 Minutes," the grieving father shared new details about his children's final moments, what Lindsay told him about the killings and the online attacks he says are hurting their legacy.

The interview aired after Lindsay's triple-murder trial ended in a mistrial. Her attorneys argued she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and was not criminally responsible, while prosecutors maintained she knew what she was doing.

From his desperate plea at the hospital to the online claims that followed the mistrial, Patrick described how the tragedy has shaped every part of his life.

PATRICK CLANCY SPEAKS OUT AFTER HUNG JURY IN LINDSAY CLANCY CASE, ADDRESSES PROSPECT OF ANOTHER TRIAL

Patrick said he clung to hope that Callan might survive after his siblings, 5-year-old Cora and 3-year-old Dawson, were found dead inside the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home.

Doctors had restored the baby's heartbeat, and Patrick told Douthat he began imagining the life he could still give his youngest child.

"I remember that night, I really thought there was a chance that Callan would live," Patrick said.

"And I remember just thinking, ‘Just give me one. Just give me one kid,’" he continued. "And I would raise him as best I could, and I would give him the best life I possibly could. And I'd tell him about his brother and sister."

Patrick said that hope faded when he reached Boston Children's Hospital and saw the look on a doctor's face.

Callan's heart continued beating for four days. Patrick became emotional as he recalled apologizing to his son and spending his final moments beside him.

"I said, ‘I'm so sorry,’" he told Douthat, his voice breaking. "And I got to hold him. I got to lay down next to him. And he died in my arms."

While Callan remained in the hospital, Patrick said he held his son's hand and used his free hand to write about all three children. He told Douthat he feared their memories might fade if he did not put them into words.

The tributes Patrick wrote also included words of forgiveness for Lindsay. He said she has never asked him to forgive her, but he chose to give that forgiveness anyway.

LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY

"I saw headlines that said, you know, ‘killer mom’ and ‘baby murderer,’ ‘monster,’ and none of them were accurate," Patrick said during the interview. "I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that."

Patrick said he also feared anger would consume him if he could not forgive her.

"I felt that if I didn't get there, I would be eaten up inside," he said.

When Patrick asked Lindsay whether she remembered killing their children, he said she described the memory as dreamlike.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

"She said it was like a dream, and she remembered it much in the way you would remember a dream after waking up," he told Douthat.

Patrick said he did the best he could as Lindsay's condition worsened but must live with what happened.

"I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time, and I live with the outcome," he said. "I live with it every day."

Patrick told Douthat his grief became so overwhelming that he questioned whether he would live to see another birthday.

"There was a time where I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday, and I was completely fine with it," he said.

Patrick later left Duxbury for New York City, where he could grieve without being recognized. Five weeks after the move, on what would have been Callan's first birthday, he went to St. Patrick's Cathedral, lit a candle and told his son, "I love you, buddy."

"And I walk out on Fifth Avenue and I start crying my eyes out, and nobody cared," Patrick recalled.

For Patrick, being able to cry without drawing attention was exactly what he needed.

"I thought, this is where I need to be," he said. "I can grieve."

His Manhattan apartment remains filled with reminders of the children, including a baby sloth Cora carried everywhere and a photograph of Callan wearing an oversized bow tie, "60 Minutes" showed.

Patrick said they also return to him in vivid dreams. In one, Cora walked into the kitchen of the family's former home and hugged him.

"I just looked at her and it was like I basically just said, ‘Where have you been?’" he recalled. "Those dreams are so real."

The mistrial unleashed what Douthat described as a "trial by TikTok," with online sleuths and influencers spreading baseless theories portraying Patrick as uncaring, unfaithful and even responsible for the children's deaths.

"It's deeply harmful to the legacy of my children," Patrick said. "It is a huge distraction from what really matters here, which is perinatal mental health, and it's done real harm to real people."

LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

He said the repeated accusations have made it painful to be in public and warned that people may start believing false claims if they see them often enough.

"After seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it," Patrick said. "And that's what we're left with."

Patrick said he sought answers from Postpartum Support International, psychiatrists and other experts. Those conversations helped him begin processing what happened.

Patrick's wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, joined him for the "60 Minutes" interview and recalled first learning about his children after noticing their photograph on his phone during a coffee outing.

"I just asked, ‘Who are those cuties?’" Danis told Douthat. "And Pat had said, ‘Those are my kids.’"

When she asked whether they lived in Massachusetts, Patrick told her they had died.

Patrick and Danis met through a New York running club in January 2024. Their relationship deepened as they continued running together, and they married in New York City this April.

The couple also discussed starting a family.

Asked what he would tell a future child about Cora, Dawson and Callan, Patrick said all of his children would remain part of the same family.

"You have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids," he said. "And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister."

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after jurors split 11-1, with 11 favoring a finding that Lindsay was not criminally responsible and one holding out for a conviction. Prosecutors have not announced whether they will try her again.

item.title: Cowboys' Cobie Durant gets stepped on in worst place possible during win over Commanders

item.title: Chad Gilbert, New Found Glory founding member and lead guitarist, dead at 45
item.description: Chad Gilbert, founding member and lead guitarist for New Found Glory, has died at the age of 45. He had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.
item.content:encoded:
Chad Gilbert, the founding member and lead guitarist for the punk rock band New Found Glory, has died. He was 45.

The band and the late musician's wife Lisa Cimorelli announced the news of Gilbert's death in a joint Instagram post Saturday. The post did not cite a cause of death, but Gilbert had battled adrenal cancer since 2021, and in February, underwent brain surgery after doctors found tumors.

"On the morning of September 20th, Chad Everett Gilbert passed away peacefully in his sleep," they wrote. "He left this world surrounded by friends and family and took his final breaths with his wife and mother by his side, just as he wished."

DUNCAN SHEIK, ‘BARELY BREATHING’ SINGER, DEAD AT 56

"We are devastated and shocked by how quickly he left us, yet so grateful for how peacefully and smoothly he went," they continued. "The amount of visitors that crowded the hospital lobby at a moment’s notice is a testament to how beloved and cherished Chad was, and always will be. He was a legendary musician, but his favorite accomplishment was being a husband and father. His biggest dreams came true. He is survived by his wife, Lisa, his daughter, Lily, his mother, Jackie, and his brother, Brian."

In their statement, New Found Glory, whose members include lead singer Jordan Pundik, bassist Ian Grushka and drummer Cyrus Bolooki, paid tribute to Gilbert’s lasting influence on the band and the deep personal bond that they shared.

"Chad’s guitar playing, songwriting, humor, and relentless drive helped shape New Found Glory for nearly three decades," they wrote. "Through more than a dozen albums, endless tours around the world, and more accolades than we ever could have imagined, Chad challenged all of us to grow as musicians, performers, and human beings."

"While we are devastated to lose him, we are so grateful for the incredible life he lived, the memories we shared, and the brotherhood we had. His influence will always be part of New Found Glory and his spirit will be felt on every stage we stand on, with every note we play."

'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE

"Rest in peace, Chad. We love you forever," they concluded.

Fox News Digital has reached out to New Found Glory's management company Le Grand Music and label Pure Noise Records for comment.

Gilbert had been open about his battle with stage 4 adrenal cancer that was first diagnosed in 2021 and later spread to his spine, lungs and brain. He was initially diagnosed with metastatic pheochromocytoma, a rare adrenal gland cancer, in which the tumor grows inside the inner part of the adrenal gland.

In a February interview with People magazine, he shared that he began experiencing weakness on the left side of his body and difficulty walking while New Found Glory was promoting its latest album "Listen Up!"

After collapsing at home, Gilbert underwent a scan and doctors discovered he had three brain tumors, one of which required emergency surgery. Gilbert later underwent radiation and immunotherapy to treat the two remaining tumors.

After the operation, he told People magazine his diagnosis changed to adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), which starts growing in the outer layer of the adrenal gland.

JOAN JETT CANCELS REMAINING 2026 CONCERTS AFTER UNDERGOING SURGERY FOR 'FRACTURED VERTEBRAE'

In a March Instagram post, Gilbert wrote that his "recovery has been bumpy at times," but that he was "feeling much better now and getting stronger by the day."

Gilbert returned to the stage in June, performing with New Found Glory during their tour stop in Nashville, Tennessee. He joined the band onstage to perform a few songs while using a mobility scooter.

"I got to play a show in front of my daughter, something I truly never thought I’d get to do again," he wrote in an Instagram post following the show. "And my beautiful wife and all the nurses and doctors, my amazing team that have kept me alive through my battle. It was very emotional getting up on stage with my band again to play. So many feelings all at once."

Gilbert shared daughter Lily, 5, with Cimorelli, whom he wed in 2020. The guitarist was previously married to Eisley singer Sherri DuPree. The two tied the knot in 2007 but split later that year. Gilbert was also married to Paramore lead singer Hayley Williams from 2016 to 2017.

Born March 9, 1981 in Coral Springs, Florida, Gilbert helped form New Found Glory in 1997. The band broke through with its 2002 album, "Sticks and Stones," which featured the hit singles "My Friends Over You" and "Head On Collision" and reached No. 4 on the Billboard 200 chart.

New Found Glory followed up with 2004's "Catalyst," which peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and produced the singles "All Downhill from Here" and "Failure’s Not Flattering."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

New Found Glory became one of the defining bands of the early-2000s pop-punk era. The band has released 12 studio albums and toured extensively around the world. Gilbert appeared on all of New Found Glory’s albums, including "Listen Up!," which came out in February.

Outside New Found Glory, Gilbert was also known for his work in hardcore, including as a vocalist for Shai Hulud and with New Found Glory’s side project International Superheroes of Hardcore. Gilbert also worked as a producer for artists including A Day to Remember, H2O and State Champs, and collaborated with Fall Out Boy.

In addition to his wife and daughter, Gilbert is survived by his mother, Jackie and his brother, Brian.

item.title: Cubs star Alex Bregman hospitalized after taking brutal foul ball to the face
item.description: Alex Bregman posted a photo showing his left eye swollen shut after a foul ball struck his face during the Cubs vs. Reds game, vowing to return.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds after being struck in the face by a foul ball while waiting in the on-deck circle.

During the top of the fourth inning at Great American Ball Park, teammate Michael Busch chopped a foul ball into the dirt near home plate. The ball jumped off the dirt and hit Bregman squarely on the left side of his face.

Bregman ran toward the visitors' dugout in visible pain while holding his face.

Medical staff escorted him to the clubhouse, and Matt Shaw entered the game to replace him at third base.

Cubs manager Craig Counsell confirmed the ball hit Bregman directly on his left cheekbone, causing a laceration under his eye, a nosebleed and swelling.

Bregman was transported to a local Cincinnati hospital for CT scans and X-rays to check for orbital and cheek fractures.

Bregman posted an update on his Instagram later on Sunday, showing his left eye swollen shut and his nose plugged, posting, "Thanks for the messages y'all. I'll be back."

Medical staff reportedly cleared him to travel back to Chicago with the team Sunday night.

Any extended absence for Bregman would impact the Cubs during a tight National League Wild Card race with one week remaining in the regular season.

If Bregman lands on the injured list, the Cubs will rely on Shaw and Pedro Ramirez at third base.

It’s another scary reminder of how fast things go wrong on the field.

item.title: Gorillaz frontman Damon Albarn holds up Palestinian flag during show after Macklemore tour removal
item.description: Gorillaz frontman Damon Albarn waved a Palestinian flag during a Florida show on Thursday in an apparent response to Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour.
item.content:encoded:
The English band Gorillaz appeared to call out the decision to boot rapper Macklemore from Ed Sheeran's tour over his call for a "Free Palestine" with a similar stunt during one of their shows last week.

While performing in Florida on Thursday, band frontman Damon Albarn held up a Palestinian flag and draped it over his shoulder while addressing the audience.

"Don’t forget this. Ever. Stand your position. Don’t ever be neutral," Albarn said.

ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT

Fox News Digital reached out to Gorillaz and Sheeran for comment.

Gorillaz is one of several performers who have used the stage to promote anti-Israel causes since the Oct. 7 terror attacks. The band previously performed at the Together for Palestine concert in 2025 for Palestinian organizations.

During the Glastonbury Festival in 2024, Albarn asked the audience whether they supported Palestine.

"Three things, and you have to show me how you feel about them: Palestine. Are you pro-Palestine? Do you feel that’s an unfair war? Okay," Albarn said.

Gorillaz's stunt came after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran's tour, causing several progressive figures to rally behind the rapper and criticize Sheeran, though Sheeran's representatives have said he was not involved in the decision.

ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO

Macklemore has since doubled down on his activism and defended his efforts to shout "Free Palestine" at his show and perform his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall."

"I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," Macklemore wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement last week. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families."

Sheeran addressed the controversy during his show on Saturday night.

ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL

"Now, I want to address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand. I’ve tried in my career to not be a political commentator of any kind because I want my music and shows to be about unity not division, about humanity not politics," Sheeran said.

He continued, "But this is a humanitarian issue and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore. What happened in Israel at a… music festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate."

item.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror makes new promise as lawyer warns of public attacks
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's mistrial juror Michael P. Desronvil plans a personal statement while her defense team pursues a double jeopardy dismissal motion.
item.content:encoded:
The lone juror who blocked a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s triple-murder trial has promised to tell his story in his own words as his attorney warns that jurors must be allowed to follow the evidence without fear of retaliation.

Attorney Edward Paltzik said Michael P. Desronvil, whose refusal to join the other 11 jurors led to a mistrial, will issue a personal statement in the "near future."

"Michael will be making a personal statement in the near future, in his own words," Paltzik wrote in a Facebook post.

Paltzik thanked those who sent emails, texts and voice messages in support of Desronvil, while acknowledging that others may disagree with the position he took inside the jury room.

CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY

"This country was built on intelligent debate in the public square," Paltzik wrote. "That’s the same reason we support the good faith right of an individual juror to follow the evidence and the law to wherever they take him or her, free from fear of reprisal."

LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE INDEFINITELY IMPOUNDS JUROR NAMES, CITING SAFETY AND 'DIVISIVE' ATTENTION

The attorney’s latest comments come as the deeply divisive case returns to the national spotlight. Patrick Clancy, the father of the three slain children and Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband, gave his first television interview on CBS News’ "60 Minutes" Sunday night.

Patrick Clancy discussed his grief, memories of his children and baseless conspiracy theories that have spread online since the January 2023 killings. His wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, also appeared in the segment with correspondent Ross Douthat.

JUDGE JUDY WARNS OF 'DANGER' IF PROSECUTORS DON'T RETRY LINDSAY CLANCY AFTER MURDER TRIAL ENDS IN MISTRIAL

Lindsay Clancy, 36, was tried on three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of the couple’s children, 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. The children were found strangled inside the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.

Clancy admitted killing the children, but her attorneys argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argued that the former labor and delivery nurse understood what she was doing and carried out the killings deliberately.

LINDSAY CLANCY JUDGE CALLS MISTRIAL, THEN GRANTS DEFENSE ONE HOUR STAY FOR APPEAL

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after seven days of deliberations. The jury was split 11-1, with 11 jurors prepared to find Clancy not criminally responsible and Desronvil holding out for a conviction.

Desronvil later said he had no doubt prosecutors proved their case.

LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS

"Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned," Desronvil said in a statement first reported by NewsNation and confirmed to Fox News Digital by Paltzik.

Desronvil said he tried to raise different theories during deliberations but was repeatedly cut off by fellow jurors who treated his questions as uncertainty.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM

The fallout from the mistrial quickly spilled beyond the courthouse, with Desronvil facing intense public scrutiny over his refusal to move off his position.

Paltzik, who previously represented President Donald Trump in lawsuits against The New York Times, CBS and ABC News, told Fox News Digital that he is focused on Desronvil’s "health, safety and well-being." He has called the juror an "American Hero" and "Champion of Justice."

LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT

Former prosecutor and behavioral health law expert Mark Astor previously told Fox News Digital that Desronvil appeared to have hired counsel to defend his name after being "dragged through the mud."

"The whole idea of the jury is sort of this sacred arena where jurors get to decide a verdict in a case," Astor said. "And now we’re taking what is really a sacred arena, and we’re exposing it to the public."

Plymouth County prosecutors have not announced whether they will retry Clancy. Her defense team has raised the possibility of resolving the case without another trial and brought in veteran Boston attorney Martin Weinberg to pursue a motion seeking dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds.

Clancy is due back in Plymouth Superior Court for a status hearing Sept. 29, when the path forward could become clearer.

Fox News Digital's Adam Sabes contributed to this report.

item.title: Jack Osbourne admits raising kids without a nanny isn’t as gnarly as he expected
item.description: Jack Osbourne and wife Aree are raising five kids with no nanny, finding a rhythm while the family navigates grief after Ozzy Osbourne's death.
item.content:encoded:

Aree, who is a stay-at-home mom, and Jack share daughters Maple, 4, and Ozzy Matilda, 6 months. Jack is also the father of Pearl, 14, Andy, 11, and Minnie, 8, whom he shares with his ex-wife, Lisa Stelly.

KELLY OSBOURNE HID WITH OZZY FOR 9 MONTHS TO AVOID BEING BODY-SHAMED WHILE PREGNANT

The couple recently marked Maple’s first day of preschool. Jack shared a photo of Maple posing alongside her baby sister and jokingly referred to Ozzy Matilda as her "emotional support squad."

item.title: Browns' Deshaun Watson may have silenced doubters after outlasting Baker Mayfield and 2-hour weather delay
item.description: Deshaun Watson threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns as the Cleveland Browns outlasted a two-hour weather delay to beat Baker Mayfield's Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns stayed in Florida after a brutal Week 1 loss that had many wondering if the embattled quarterback’s job was at stake as the team’s starter.

With a comeback in the second half, and waiting patiently for a two-hour weather delay at Raymond James Stadium, the Browns defeated Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-19, to squash that talk for now.

Lightning, high winds and torrential downpour were always on the cards while looking at the forecast this week in Tampa, but it hit at the worst possible time after the Browns took their first lead of the game after a six-minute drive that resulted in a Blake Whiteheart 17-yard touchdown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Mayfield, trying to have a bit of a revenge game against the team that drafted him first overall and later released him in favor of Watson, whom Cleveland had just traded for, needed to respond with a touchdown drive of his own.

The Buccaneers were desperate to do so after falling on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals the week prior, where Mayfield had trouble with turnovers throughout the contest.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, at the two-minute warning, a lightning delay was called as the forecast showed a large system rolling through that would impact Raymond James Stadium, and boy, did it.

The weather had both teams in the locker rooms for over two hours, as play was stuck at second-and-4 from Cleveland’s 28-yard line.

Finally, when play resumed, the Bucs started off nicely with Bucky Irving picking up a first down. But as the rain continued to come down, the Browns’ defense turned up the heat on Mayfield.

A costly holding penalty on second-and-4 pushed Mayfield and the offense back to Cleveland’s 23-yard line. From there, Mayfield was unable to hook up with any of his receivers, including a final heave to the end zone where the ball was out of reach for Emeka Egbuka.

Watson and the Browns celebrated on the sideline, and they did so with head coach Todd Monken, who secured his first career win as Cleveland’s head coach.

Watson finished the game 24-of-30 for 238 yards and two passing touchdowns, the first of which to rookie Denzel Boston, who finished with a game-high 95 yards on five catches.

The Browns are finally hosting their home opener next week against the Carolina Panthers, and after the jeers the crowd gave Watson during the preseason, it will be interesting to see his reception now, assuming he remains the starter.

This performance, a marked improvement over the 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, should be enough to secure Watson's position as the team's starting quarterback.

Meanwhile, after an inauspicious start, the Buccaneers remain at home next week to face the Minnesota Vikings, whose defense stymied the Chicago Bears in their own weather-laden bout on Sunday.

item.title: Caitlin Clark shines, but Fever suffer embarrassing blowout loss to Mystics as playoff race heats up

item.title: Washington Commanders face season-defining crisis as Jayden Daniels suffers another serious elbow injury
item.description: Jayden Daniels was carted off at halftime after appearing to dislocate his left elbow on the final play of the half against the Dallas Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field at halftime during Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys after he appeared to injure his left elbow on the final play of the first half.

During the play, Daniels seemed to hyperextend the left elbow. And, yes, it was ugly.

It happened on the final play of the first half when Daniels pulled away from center but tripped. As he tried to regain his balance, he used his left arm to hold himself up.

COMMANDERS OFFENSE TAKES MAJOR HIT AS STAR OFFENSIVE TACKLE SUFFERS MAJOR TRAINING CAMP INJURY

The elbow gave way in a manner it is not supposed to bend.

KYLER MURRAY KNOCKED OUT OF VIKINGS DEBUT AFTER FOREARM TO THE HELMET AND BLOW TO NECK BY TWO PACKERS

After the game, coach Dan Quinn told reporters Daniels had indeed dislocated his elbow. But X-rays showed no fracture. But it is clear that even after an MRI test on Monday, Daniels will miss time.

Marcus Mariota will take the reins at quarterback until Daniels can return.

"We will rally so hard around Marcus until, you know, Jayden's back," Quinn said.

And all this is terrible news because Daniels had a similar injury in 2025 against the Seattle Seahawks.

So this very easily could be a season-defining injury for Daniels. And the Commanders.

Again.

OutKick medical expert Dr. David Chao, who served 17 seasons as the head physician for the then-San Diego Chargers and currently runs the Sports Injury Central website, studied the injury via tape. He put out a post on X with his view.

"By video, clear left elbow dislocation...

"Similar to last season

"Joint comes out easier second time original ligament tear heals "looser."

Although the injury was to his arm, Daniels was carted off to the locker room. He wore a towel over his head, apparently, to avoid showing his facial reaction to the crowd.

And if the MRI results show what everyone's eyes saw, the Washington Commanders' season is on the brink in only the second week of the season.

If Daniels faces a similar situation to last season, he faces a similar rehabilitation.

Daniels dislocated his left elbow while scrambling in Washington’s Week 9 loss to Seattle on Nov. 2, 2025. An MRI found no fracture or ligament damage, so he avoided surgery and was not placed on injured reserve.

The Commanders managed a 2-6 record in games Mariota started in place of Daniels last season, and they didn't rally to win on Sunday.

He returned in Week 14 against Minnesota but aggravated the elbow, was not cleared for the following game and was shut down for the final three weeks of the season as the Commanders prioritized his recovery for 2026.

That recovery appears to be derailed, at least for the short term.

"I didn't see him until postgame," Quinn said when asked about how Daniels was handling his terrible luck. "But it was hard. It was quiet and you know, emotional in that space, knowing how much he's put into his return."

item.title: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
item.description: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead.

The Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime, with Trey Smack kicking a 26-yard field goal to complete the comeback.

Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. Geno Smith connected with Garrett Wilson for a 5-yard score in the third quarter to give New York a 14-7 lead.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Jets appeared to have delivered the knockout blow early in the fourth quarter when they recovered a Lloyd fumble at the Green Bay 18-yard line. But the offense couldn't move the ball and settled for a 32-yard Jason Sanders field goal, extending the lead to 17-7 with 11:04 remaining.

That's when everything started to unravel.

A 38-yard pass-interference penalty helped Green Bay march down the field before Love found Christian Watson for a 3-yard touchdown. The Jets failed to pick up a first down on their next possession, and Skyy Moore returned the ensuing punt 63 yards to the New York 19-yard line. Smack kicked a 34-yard field goal four plays later to tie the game.

New York still had a chance to win in regulation. After Breece Hall gained just one yard on third-and-2, the Jets faced fourth-and-1 at midfield with 1:20 remaining. Aaron Glenn kept his offense on the field rather than punting, an aggressive decision to try to win the game. It's hard to fault Glenn for trusting his offense to gain one yard, but Braelon Allen was stuffed. Green Bay failed to capitalize, sending the game to overtime.

The Jets received the ball first in overtime and the possession was a complete disaster. The Packers sacked Smith on consecutive plays, the offense committed a false-start penalty and New York faced a third-and-30 from their own 10-yard line before eventually punting on fourth down.

Green Bay then moved 58 yards on four offensive plays, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Jarvis Brownlee Jr., before Smack ended the game on the fifth play of the drive.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penalties were a problem for both teams throughout the game. Green Bay was flagged 14 times for 133 yards, while New York committed 13 penalties for 156 yards. That's an absurd 27 accepted penalties for 289 yards.

But the timing of the Jets' two biggest penalties proved especially costly: the 38-yard pass-interference call aided Green Bay's fourth-quarter touchdown drive, while Brownlee's 15-yard penalty moved the Packers into position for the winning field goal.

Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. It wasn't a spectacular performance, but it should have been good enough given how well New York's defense played.

That's what makes the loss particularly brutal for the Jets. New York outgained Green Bay 285-199, held the Packers to 1-of-9 on third down, won the turnover battle and possessed the ball for nearly 11 minutes longer. Love threw for just 145 yards, although he threw two touchdowns and avoided turning the ball over.

The Jets had the game won and a chance to send the MetLife Stadium crowd home believing in a 2-0 team. Instead, they gave the game away and sent their fans home wondering how they managed to blow another one.

item.title: Mike Vrabel snaps at reporter over Drake Maye's struggles after Pats win: 'you're not going to ruin my Sunday'
item.description: Mike Vrabel told reporters they wouldn't ruin his Sunday after the Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3, but Drake Maye's struggles still loom large.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots got their first win of the season Sunday, and head coach Mike Vrabel wasn't about to let a few perfectly valid questions about his quarterback spoil the celebration.

After New England defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3, Vrabel had a tense exchange with Boston Globe reporter Ben Volin, who pressed him about his level of concern over Drake Maye's performance through the first two weeks of the season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Vrabel wasn't interested in entertaining the question.

"You're not going to ruin my Sunday," the coach fired back.

The exchange continued when reporter Greg Bedard also questioned Vrabel about Maye's struggles, prompting the coach to make it clear that he wasn't going to dwell on the negatives after a victory.

To be fair, though, the reporters had a legitimate reason to ask.

Maye hasn't exactly looked like the quarterback who led New England to the Super Bowl last season, and Sunday's win over Pittsburgh did little to put those concerns to rest.

The 23-year-old completed 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, no touchdowns and one interception against the Steelers. While he connected with receiver Romeo Doubs for a 63-yard gain, the Patriots struggled to consistently move the ball and finished with just 13 offensive points.

Instead, New England's defense did most of the heavy lifting, holding Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers to just 3 points and 235 total yards.

Rookie running back TreVeyon Henderson provided the Patriots' only offensive touchdown with a 39-yard run in the first quarter. Later, Christian Barmore strip-sacked Rodgers, and Elijah Ponder returned the fumble 19 yards for a touchdown to put the game away.

In other words, the Patriots won comfortably, but Maye wasn't exactly the reason why.

Sunday's performance came just 11 days after a disastrous season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.

In a rematch of Super Bowl LX, Maye threw three fourth-quarter interceptions as New England blew a 10-point lead and lost 13-10. His final interception came in the end zone with just 26 seconds remaining, ending a potential game-tying drive.

Maye finished that game with 178 passing yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. Afterward, he acknowledged that he had abandoned the patient approach that had worked earlier in the game.

"We had the game under control," Maye said following the loss. "Thought we had a good plan to start chipping away and be patient and lost patience, and it cost us, decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end."

Through two games, Maye has thrown four interceptions and just one touchdown pass.

That's a far cry from his 2025 campaign, when he threw for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns while finishing as the runner-up in NFL MVP voting.

Vrabel is certainly entitled to enjoy Sunday's victory, especially after the Patriots' ugly collapse against Seattle.

Sure, the season is young. No need to overreact.

But with New England's franchise quarterback — so far — struggling to recapture last year's form, the questions about his performance aren't going away simply because Vrabel wants them to.

item.title: Converse pulls latest shoes ad after critics accuse of sharing 'racist' and 'reckless' KKK imagery
item.description: Converse pulled a shoe ad last week after critics said the imagery resembled a Ku Klux Klan hood and a lynching victim, prompting a public apology and statement.
item.content:encoded:
Converse apologized and pulled a shoe ad last week that some claimed featured Ku Klux Klan imagery.

The ad, which has been removed from the Nike subsidiary's social media pages, featured K-pop singer Karina of the girl group aespa promoting the Chuck 70 X and Run Star Crush sneakers. In the ad, Karina held a pair of black high-top shoes under a star-shaped spotlight while wearing a long white skirt.

Several social media users asserted that Karina resembled a KKK member, with the shoes resembling a lynching victim. Critics included Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., who released a statement on the ad on Friday.

OUTKICK'S CRAIG CARTON REVEALS THE REAL REASON NIKE STOCK IS IN THE TANK: 'THEY'RE FAILING MISERABLY'

"Nike and Converse, what the hell were you thinking?" Carter said. "Your campaign shows what looks like a hooded Klansman, framed by what appears to be the dangling feet of a lynching victim. There is nothing creative or artistic about it. It is racist, reckless and deeply offensive."

After facing backlash, Converse eventually pulled the ad and released a statement apologizing for the campaign.

TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW

"We’re sorry. We understand why this image is deeply upsetting and recognize that we got this wrong. We removed it from our channels and are working to remove it everywhere it appeared. This should not have happened, and we will do better," the statement sent to Fox News Digital read.

This latest ad backlash comes as Nike is set to be removed from the S&P 100 after nearly 18 years, following its value dropping by more than $200 billion since 2021.

Conservative critics have frequently accused Nike of embracing woke politics by partnering with progressive figures like Colin Kaepernick and Dylan Mulvaney. However, Nike has faced backlash from the left as well.

NIKE FORGOT THAT REPUBLICANS BUY SNEAKERS, TOO, AND NOW IT'S GETTING BOOTED FROM THE S&P 100

In April, Nike went viral with a Boston Marathon ad reading "Runners welcome. Walkers tolerated" which critics claimed was "pace-shaming" participants.

In a new comment to Fox News Digital, a Carter spokesperson said that the apology was not enough.

"An apology and the removal of the images are not enough. Nike and Converse must explain how this campaign was conceived and approved, identify those responsible, and commission an independent investigation. They must also disclose the process and establish safeguards to ensure that imagery invoking the Klan and the lynching of Black people is never approved again," Carter's office said.

item.title: Atlanta Falcons are dealing with the worst quarterback situation in the NFL and it isn't even close
item.description: Cooper Rush fumbled and threw two interceptions before Kevin Stefanski benched him, and his replacement threw a pick six in his Falcons debut.
item.content:encoded:
The worst quarterback situation in the NFL right now? The Atlanta Falcons.

And it isn't very close at all.

The Falcons on Sunday started third-stringer Cooper Rush for the second time this season while Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa were designated as inactive due to ongoing health issues.

Penix Jr. has been recovering from knee surgery following an ACL injury last season.

FALCONS QUARTERBACK PROBLEMS DEEPEN AS TUA TAGOVAILOA SUFFERS OBLIQUE STRAIN AT PRACTICE

And Tagovailoa was out for the second consecutive week after he suffered an unexpected oblique injury two weeks ago, this time in practice. Although no one touched him.

Anyway, Rush got the call and he promptly stunk.

Again.

On Atlanta's opening possession, Rush lost the ball on a fumble, which the Panthers recovered at the Atlanta 35-yard line. Carolina converted the turnover into a touchdown.

Rush threw an interception on the following series, then added a second one later in the game.

He completed 10 of 17 passes against the Panthers, which doesn't sound terrible except that you read the previous paragraphs that outlined Rush's, ahem, struggles with turnovers.

This followed a Week 1 performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers in which Rush also threw two interceptions.

"Obviously, extremely disappointed in that game and extremely disappointed in how that game started," Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. "And then [we] could not crawl out of that hole. And in the second half, it got away from us. So very disappointed.

"As you guys know, giveaways and takeaways are the key to this game and to turn it over that many times ... there's no way to win in the NFL like that."

Stefanski made those feelings known before he ever stepped up to the post-game microphones. Because he benched Rush before the end of the third quarter.

The coach had seen enough. Except the poor quarterback play was far from over.

Stefanski inserted fourth-string quarterback Jack Strand.

Strand threw an interception on his first pass attempt. And it wasn't just any interception. Strand threw a pick six when Devin Lloyd returned his pass 16 yards for a score.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This is Keystone Cops type QB play. The Falcons are used to QB issues, but this is something else again.

The Falcons are hoping that can end by Thursday when they play the Green Bay Packers.

They're hoping Penix Jr., who has been practicing and ramping up toward game action, can start that in Wisconsin. They hope that Tagovailoa will ultimately decide he can tolerate some pain and take the field, or receive an injection to help him do so.

The Falcons are doing a lot of hoping about their quarterback room. And so far, it hasn't paid off.

item.title: Jalen Hurts saves Eagles from ugly upset as Philadelphia escapes Titans to remain unbeaten
item.description: Jalen Hurts hit Darius Cooper for a last-second touchdown to erase a three-point deficit as the Philadelphia Eagles escaped Nashville 24-20.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles moved to 2-0 with a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

That's a sentence most football fans expected to read before the game even started. What most probably didn't expect was exactly what it took for the Eagles to go into Nissan Stadium and beat the Titans.

Jalen Hurts connected with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with less than 10 seconds remaining to turn a 20-17 Tennessee lead into a 24-20 Philadelphia victory. The Titans, who looked completely lost last week in a 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, had the reigning NFC East champions on the ropes for much of the afternoon.

Philadelphia's problems started immediately. Star running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger on the Eagles' first offensive play and spent most of the first half on the sideline. He returned after halftime wearing a neck roll, but finished with just four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That opening possession lasted more than seven minutes and moved deep into Tennessee territory, but it ended in the worst possible way. Hurts tried to find DeVonta Smith in the end zone, but Amani Hooker intercepted the pass and returned it 92 yards to the Philadelphia 10-yard line. Four plays later, Cam Ward scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak to give Tennessee a 7-0 lead.

The Eagles responded with a 2-yard touchdown run from Tank Bigsby and Hurts connected with Smith for a 22-yard touchdown late in the second quarter. But the Titans refused to go away. Joey Slye kicked a 37-yard field goal just as time expired in the first half, cutting Philadelphia's lead to 14-10.

Jake Elliott extended the lead with a 58-yard field goal in the third quarter, but Ward scored his second rushing touchdown of the game to tie the score at 17.

Philadelphia had an opportunity to take control in the fourth quarter, but Hurts threw his second interception with just over six minutes remaining. The Titans responded with a 69-yard drive that included a 41-yard completion from Ward to Elic Ayomanor and a 27-yard run by Tyjae Spears on third-and-22.

The Eagles' defense eventually held Tennessee to a 33-yard field goal, but that still gave the Titans a three-point lead with 1:56 remaining and Philadelphia had no timeouts.

That's when Hurts finally looked like the quarterback who led the Eagles to a Super Bowl victory in February 2025.

The 28-year-old signal-caller converted a third-and-6 with a 20-yard completion to Dontayvion Wicks and connected with Smith three times for 34 yards on the drive. Smith's final catch was a sweet grab along the sideline where he barely got his second foot down inbounds. The crucial play went for 19 yards and set the Eagles up at the Tennessee 3-yard line with 20 seconds remaining.

Two plays later, Hurts found Cooper for the game-winning touchdown, the first touchdown catch of Cooper’s NFL career.

Hurts finished 26-of-37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown, accounting for nearly half of Philadelphia's passing production. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Smith has to step up as the team's top receiver, and he looked the part against Tennessee.

AJ BROWN SAYS THERE'S BEEN SILENCE BETWEEN HIM AND EX-TEAMMATE JALEN HURTS SINCE HIS MOVE TO NEW ENGLAND

Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards and didn't turn the ball over, while adding both of Tennessee's touchdowns on the ground. It wasn't an especially good performance for the Titans offense, as the Eagles outgained Tennessee 341-291 and out-possessed the Titans by nearly 13 minutes.

The problem for Hurts and the Eagles was the two turnovers and general sloppy play at key moments.

Obviously, it’s hard to panic about a team that won its first two games. But if I were an Eagles fan, I’d feel about as nervous as possible for someone whose team is 2-0.

Philadelphia has beaten Washington and Tennessee by a combined six points. The Commanders might be better than people expected, but the Titans entered Sunday looking like one of the worst teams in football. The Eagles needed a touchdown with nine seconds remaining to beat them.

Good teams find ways to win close games, and Hurts deserves credit for helping the team survive back-to-back upset bids. But a supposed NFC contender cannot continue playing like this and expect to keep escaping.

The standings say the Eagles are perfect. Their play on the field has been anything but.

item.title: McDonald’s once sold beloved cookies featuring forgotten characters from the chain's past
item.description: McDonald's discontinued McDonaldland Cookies featured Grimace and Ronald McDonald faces with a subtle lemon flavor that fans still crave decades later.
item.content:encoded:
Introduced in 1974, McDonaldland Cookies became a regular addition to McDonald’s Happy Meals when they debuted nationwide in 1979.

But the beloved menu item was discontinued in the early 2000s, to the disappointment of many fans.

The small, crunchy cookies were baked for McDonald’s by Keebler, had a subtle lemon flavor and featured the faces of beloved McDonald’s characters like Grimace, Ronald McDonald, Birdie and Hamburglar.

MCDONALD'S REVIVES DECADES-OLD FAVORITE FOR AMERICA 250 AFTER YEARS OF CUSTOMER REQUESTS

Customers described them as a cross between shortbread and animal crackers.

McDonaldland Cookies came in either a little plastic bag or a brightly colored cardboard box that also showed the faces of McDonald’s characters.

The fast food chain altered its Happy Meals to include healthier items such as apple slices in the early 2000s.

Between 2003 and 2004, McDonaldland Cookies were discontinued at all U.S. locations.

Chocolate chip cookies, however, remained on the menu.

McDonald’s has been serving some variation of chocolate chip cookies since the early 1970s, with today's chewy, soft-baked version introduced in 2012.

MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT

Although McDonaldland Cookies are no longer available in the United States, select McDonald’s locations in Australia still offer them, and certain New Zealand restaurants serve the treat under the name "McHappy Cookies."

Fans have also shared on Reddit that a cookie with a flavor and texture similar to the original McDonaldland cookies is available at Aldi supermarkets.

McDonaldland Cookies might be gone in the U.S. — but the characters have not been totally forgotten.

item.title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
item.description: Massage flu symptoms like soreness, fatigue and headaches are real, but experts debunk the popular claim that massages release toxins from the body.
item.content:encoded:
A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches.

Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness.

The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis.

DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH

"This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital.

"The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently."

Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added.

"Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said.

Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover."

"The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media."

A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments.

"This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this."

Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes.

To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Voelsch also suggested drinking water, eating something light beforehand and moving gently afterward.

Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor.

"If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said.

Voelsch recommended seeking medical advice if symptoms last longer than about 72 hours or include fever, sharp or radiating pain, numbness or tingling, spreading swelling or bruising, or faintness.
